text: In modern AI/GPU systems, the classic 'memory wall' has evolved into what problem?
choices: Transistors have become too slow to switch
The interconnect bottleneck: compute throughput vastly exceeds the bandwidth available to move data between chips and to memory
Lasers have become too expensive to manufacture
Software cannot use more than a single core
explanation: The bottleneck is now moving data, not computing: a GPU may have ~10^15 FLOP/s of compute but far less bandwidth to feed it, so hardware sits idle waiting for data. Transistor speed, laser cost, and single-threaded software are not the defining wall described here.
